correctness.rationale: The ten two-subset vertices and 15 disjointness edges are explicitly reconstructed. The standalone standard-library code confirms cone vertices for all 121 fault sets of cardinality at most two; a complete 120-permutation, nine-orbit disjoint partition of all 455 three-edge sets; all ten disconnected cases; complete radius-two face sets of each of the eight connected representatives; valid face-to-coface matching pairs; and absence of directed cycles in all reversed Hasse diagrams. Critical cells are exactly one vertex plus 0, 1 or 4 two-cells, with no one-cells or higher critical cells. Finite discrete Morse theory gives the claimed integral homotopy types; independent mod-two chain ranks are compatible. No unverified infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The Petersen graph is a canonical diameter-two, highly symmetric cubic graph. Its intact radius-two vertex Rips complex is a simplex, so the first link-deletion budget at which new second-dimensional topology appears is a natural robustness invariant. The complete classification of all 455 minimal candidate faults identifies 60 single-sphere and five four-sphere configurations (the sharp maximum) and distinguishes them from 380 contractible connected faults. The result is a complete, interpretable integral homotopy classification at a meaningful minimal threshold, not an arbitrary parameter slice or a re-tabulation of known Betti numbers.
